quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Why is a flat front tire especially dangerous?

options.text: It affects how you steer.
The front tire powers the bike, so you will lose speed.
The flat tire will shake the bike and make it hard to use the mirrors.
You won't be able to use the brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: It affects how you steer.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire is especially dangerous because it affects your ability to steer. If your front tire goes flat while riding, safely leave the road as quickly as possible.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle operator improve visibility?

options.text: Wear dark-colored clothing.
Turn off the headlight.
Follow another vehicle very closely.
Wear bright-colored clothing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright-colored clothing.
questions.explanation: To be more visible to other road users, wear bright-colored clothing with reflective materials. Use your headlight at all times. Use your signals and brake light properly.

questions.question: When riding in a group, motorcyclists should:

options.text: Not worry about space cushions.
Increase their space cushions.
Reduce their space cushions by half.
Maintain an adequate space cushion.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maintain an adequate space cushion.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, stay close together but keep enough space around each rider for safety.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves over rain grooves or bridge gratings, you should:

options.text: Brake suddenly.
Steer in a weaving pattern.
Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
Move to the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles may weave over rain grooves or bridge gratings, but this is usually not dangerous. If your motorcycle weaves, relax and continue straight at a steady speed. Trying to zigzag will only make it more dangerous.

questions.question: When preparing to pass a vehicle on the left, you should:

options.text: Ride in the right part of your lane.
Ride in the left part of your lane.
Get as close as possible to the vehicle in front of you.
Not signal so you don't distract the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the left part of your lane.
questions.explanation: When passing on the left, ride in the left part of your lane. Signal your intention and check for traffic. Pass when safe, then signal and return to your lane when traffic allows.

questions.question: What do approved helmets do?

options.text: Limit the view of the operator.
Allow the operator to see as far to the sides as needed.
Are dangerous to wear.
Do not need to be worn if they limit your view.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow the operator to see as far to the sides as needed.
questions.explanation: Some people worry that helmets limit vision, but this is not true. Approved helmets allow operators to see as far to the sides as needed for safe riding.

questions.question: Where is there the greatest risk of conflict between a motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: Intersections
Highways
Parking lots
Residential areas

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersections
questions.explanation: The greatest risk of conflict with other vehicles happens at intersections. Be extra alert where another vehicle may cross your path.

questions.question: You should choose a lane position that:

options.text: Minimizes your space cushion and lets others see you.
Maximizes your space cushion and lets others see you.
Maximizes hazards and lets other vehicles pass you.
Minimizes hazards and lets you follow other vehicles closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maximizes your space cushion and lets others see you.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It helps you avoid wind from other vehicles, blind spots, and road hazards. Your position should discourage others from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if needed. Choose a position that maximizes your space cushion.

questions.question: Curved mirrors make cars appear:

options.text: Larger.
Farther away.
Faster.
Narrower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away.
questions.explanation: Curved mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors, but they make objects look farther away than they really are.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance:

options.text: If the pavement is slippery.
If traffic is light.
If you can see through vehicles ahead to check traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: If the pavement is slippery.
questions.explanation: You need more space if your motorcycle takes longer to stop. Increase your distance if the pavement is slippery, if you cannot see ahead, or if traffic is heavy. Keep at least a four-second gap.

questions.question: At a blind intersection with a stop sign, what should you do?

options.text: Stop at the sign and proceed through the intersection.
Ignore the sign and move forward to see better.
Stop at the sign, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic better.
Go through without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the sign, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic better.
questions.explanation: Stop where the sign tells you to. Then move forward a little and stop again just before the crossing lane. Lean forward and look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes to check for traffic. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while looking.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, you should:

options.text: Stay where the driver can see you.
Always ride on the far left of your lane.
Not worry about where you position yourself.
Always ride on the far right of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay where the driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane behind a car. This position is most visible in the car's rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: If another vehicle is following you too closely, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Move onto the shoulder.
Let the other driver pass you.
Exit the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the other driver pass you.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them ahead of you. If you can do so safely, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may make the danger worse by encouraging them to tailgate at a higher speed.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Ride in the part of your lane that lets other drivers see you as early as possible.
Always use the left lane to stay away from oncoming traffic.
Slowly creep up to the intersection.
Weave slightly so your headlight is more likely to be noticed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the part of your lane that lets other drivers see you as early as possible.
questions.explanation: Position yourself in the part of your lane where oncoming drivers will see you first. For example, at a blind corner to your right, ride on the left side of your lane, not the center.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: A passenger should never:

options.text: Wear a helmet.
Lean when the rider leans.
Wear tight clothing.
Ride sidesaddle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride sidesaddle.
questions.explanation: In South Carolina, passengers under 21 must wear a helmet and eye protection. All riders should wear these for safety. Passengers should avoid loose clothing that could catch on the motorcycle and should lean with the rider in turns. Passengers must never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, you should:

options.text: Use the brake on the good tire.
Use the brake on the flat tire.
Use both brakes.
Do not use either brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the brake on the good tire.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, slowly use the brake on the tire that is still good, if you are sure which one that is.

questions.question: Safe riders know they are safest when they are:

options.text: Seen by other motorists.
Faster than other vehicles.
On the side of the road.
On the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Seen by other motorists.
questions.explanation: Safe riders know they are safest when other drivers can clearly see them. Use your headlight, brake light, turn signals, and lane position to be as visible as possible.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding and you must stop, the best thing to do is:

options.text: Relax your grip on the handlebars.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire fails, grip the handlebars firmly and slow down by easing off the throttle while staying straight. If you must brake, slowly use the brake on the good tire, if you are sure which one that is. Move toward the side of the road as you slow down. Squeeze the clutch and stop.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Signs that show rules, like speed limits, are usually rectangular with white background and black letters or symbols. Riders must follow these rules.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you avoid road hazards.
Help you stay out of other drivers' blind spots.
Help you avoid being seen by other drivers.
Make it easier for others to see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you avoid being seen by other drivers.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see and be seen. It keeps you out of blind spots, helps you avoid hazards, shows other drivers your plans, protects you from wind blasts, and gives you an escape route if needed.

questions.question: Goggles can:

options.text: Protect your eyes and your face.
Protect your face but not your eyes.
Protect your eyes, but not your face.
Protect neither your face nor your eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect your eyes, but not your face.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes only. A face shield is needed to protect your entire face during a crash.

questions.question: When entering a curve, a group should:

options.text: Ride in a single-file line.
Ride in a staggered line.
Ride in pairs.
Ride on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a single-file line.
questions.explanation: A staggered line is usually best, but switch to single-file when turning, going through curves, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: The center of a lane often has an oily strip. This strip:

options.text: Is never safe for motorcyclists.
Is usually safe for motorcyclists, unless it rains.
Should always be avoided since other parts of the lane are safer.
Improves traction for most motorcycle tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is usually safe for motorcyclists, unless it rains.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in the center of traffic lanes. The surface is usually safe for motorcycles when dry. The strip is often only two feet wide, so you can ride to one side of it and still be in the center part of the lane.

questions.question: Reflective material on your helmet:

options.text: Helps other drivers see you.
Is not allowed.
Should only be used at night.
Does not help other drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Reflective material on a vest or helmet sides makes you more visible to other drivers. Use it day and night.
